audited_scope: New Section 6 endpoint extension, supplementing the existing complete Sections 1-5 audit
checks: Independently rechecked complete Section 6 in addition to the earlier Sections 1-5 audit. At half-volume and a boundary centroid, the nonnegative moment chain forces m=a and S=da. Thus the positive half-body equals the inscribed simplex.

Equality in the one-crossing first-moment inequality implies equality of the negative section density with the comparison cone almost everywhere: the signed weighted integrand has one sign and zero integral. Its support length is the cone height. An extreme point at that height and the common base facet span a contained simplex of the whole negative-half volume, forcing equality of bodies.

The whole body is consequently a hull of at most d+2 vertices. A nontrivial pyramid frustum has two disjoint supporting faces, each with at least d extreme points, hence at least 2d extreme points. The contradiction is strict for every d>=3, including nonpolyhedral bases.

At qv=beta, if the bad centroid cap has more than Gamma v volume, the original strict-volume argument applies. Equality makes the body a pyramid and the retained body its nontrivial base-side frustum. Every missed source of volume at least half this frustum contains its centroid in its interior, preserving full strict-source credit.

The endpoint score remains (1-q^2v)/2>Gamma. For d=3 the exact difference is 3/512. No endpoint extension is asserted in d=2, where 2d>d+2 fails. The equality geometry is fully proved rather than inferred from weak centroid containment.
